# Esther Chapter 5 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folio 457v | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/EST_005_page_001.jpg

---

**5:1** On the third day — the fast complete — Esther dressed in her royal robes and walked into the inner court of the palace, directly facing the king's throne room. The king was sitting on his throne, facing the entrance.

**5:2** The moment the king saw Queen Esther standing in the court, his face softened. He held out the golden scepter toward her. Esther stepped forward and touched its tip.

**5:3** "What is it, Queen Esther?" the king asked. "What do you want? Ask for anything — up to half my kingdom — and it's yours."

**5:4** Esther said, "If it please Your Majesty, I would like the king and Haman to come today to a banquet I've prepared."

**5:5** "Get Haman immediately," the king ordered, "so we can do what Esther asks." And the king and Haman came to Esther's banquet.

**5:6** Over the wine, the king pressed her again: "Now tell me — what is it you really want? Name it. Even half the kingdom. It's yours."

**5:7** Esther answered carefully: "What I want — what I truly ask —

**5:8** is this: if the king looks on me with favor, and if it please Your Majesty to grant what I ask, then let the king and Haman come again tomorrow to another banquet I will prepare. And then — tomorrow — I will give the king my answer."

**5:9** Haman left the banquet that day walking on air, beaming with satisfaction. But then he passed through the king's gate and saw Mordecai — who did not stand, did not flinch, did not acknowledge him at all. Instantly, Haman was consumed with fury.

**5:10** He held himself together until he got home. Then he called over his wife Zeresh and gathered all his friends.

**5:11** He bragged to them about his enormous wealth, his many sons, and every promotion and honor the king had showered on him — how he had been elevated above every other official in the empire.

**5:12** "And that's not all," Haman said. "Queen Esther herself held a private banquet today, and the only people she invited were the king and me. And she's invited me again tomorrow — just me and the king!"

**5:13** He paused. "But none of it means anything to me. Every time I see that Jew Mordecai sitting at the king's gate, it makes my blood boil."

**5:14** His wife Zeresh and all his friends had a suggestion: "Have a pole built — seventy-five feet tall. First thing in the morning, ask the king for permission to have Mordecai impaled on it. Then you can go to the queen's banquet in a good mood." Haman loved the idea, and he had the pole constructed that very night.

---

## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

1. **Esther's Masterful Strategy:** Esther does not blurt out her request. She has risked her life to enter the throne room, the king has offered her half the kingdom — and she asks him to dinner. Then at dinner, when pressed again, she asks him to come to another dinner. This is not hesitation; it is strategy. By delaying, she draws the king deeper into curiosity, commitment, and emotional investment. She also gives providence time to work — and as chapter 6 will reveal, what happens between the two banquets changes everything.

2. **The Volatility of Haman:** In a single verse (5:9), Haman swings from elation to rage. He has been honored beyond imagination — sole dinner guest of the queen alongside the king — yet one man's refusal to bow destroys his happiness entirely. This is the portrait of a man whose ego is so fragile that no amount of honor can satisfy it. The narrator is building toward his fall with exquisite psychological detail.

3. **The Pole for Mordecai:** The fifty-cubit pole (about 75 feet) is absurdly, grotesquely tall — a monument to Haman's vanity and cruelty. It is meant not just to execute but to humiliate, to make Mordecai's death a spectacle visible across Susa. In the Bible's moral logic, such overreach is always the precursor to reversal. The reader is meant to sense already that this pole will serve a different purpose than intended.

*— PNEUMA*
